correctness.rationale: For each full-dimensional Euclidean d-simplex d>=3 (n=d+1), independent uniform barycentric Dirichlet(1,...,1) samples yield E||X-Y||²=2S/[n(n+1)] and an exact fourth moment in Gram invariants S=tr G, T=tr G², H=sum G_ii². Subtracting its regular value gives the positive defect K-kappa=A||G-(S/(n-1))J||_F²/S²+B sum_i(G_ii-S/n)²/S², A=2(n²+3n+3)/((n+2)(n+3)), B=3n(n+1)/((n+2)(n+3)); this forces the unique regular-simplex minimum kappa=n(n+1)(n+6)/((n-1)(n+2)(n+3)). The nonstandard centered quartic inequality sum a_i^4 <= ((n²-3n+3)/(n(n-1)))(sum a_i²)^2 follows via Lagrange stationarity, ruling out three root values by constrained second variation, then optimizing two-level multiplicities. Along with T<=S², it identifies the unique rank-one spike upper-limit U=6n³/((n-1)(n+2)(n+3)); rank n-1 excludes upper attainment. Regular-to-spike positive definite Gram interpolation realizes all [kappa,U). Edge quadratic forms bound shape deviation with optimal 1/2 exponent from trace-zero perturbations. Independently checked Dirichlet/Gram defect interpolation exact fractions n=4..11 and all two-level multiplicities; finite checks are not proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Anderson–Goyal–Rademacher use simplex distribution moments to learn the simplex, without optimizing K over full-dimensional d>=3 shapes. Reichenwallner gives random chord moment formulas for a triangle (d=2), excluded here. Nikolov–Rafailov optimize a single moving point distance sum against regular polytope vertices, not a pair of independent interior points and all shapes.
